item.title: India opens deepwater oil, gas bids, offers to fund up to 50% of well costs
item.description: The government is rolling out a special licensing round for deepwater and ultra-deepwater oil and gas blocks, offering monthly bidding windows and relaxed fiscal terms as it prepares to shoulder up to 50 per cent of eligible exploratory well costs under its Rs 84,084-crore Samudra Manthan offshore exploration programme. The special round under the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) is aimed at accelerating exploration in India's offshore frontier basins by lowering entry barriers, sharing the high costs and risks of deepwater drilling, and making acreage available to investors throughout the year. "Under the government's 'Samudra Manthan' National Offshore Exploration Scheme, a Special OALP is being introduced for fast-track award of deepwater and ultra-deepwater (DW/UDW) exploration blocks," the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) said in a notice. DGH said details of the bid round will be announced shortly. The Special OALP is a key licensing and investment facilitation .

item.title: India, EU discuss FTA implementation issues ahead of signing in December
item.description: India and the European Union have discussed implementation issues of the free trade agreement (FTA), which is scheduled for signing in December, an official statement said on Monday. The issues were discussed during the visit of Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agarwal to Brussels last week. Agrawal met with Ditte Juul Jorgensen from the Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security; Koen Doens from the Directorate-General for International Partnerships; and Gerassimos Thomas from the Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union, European Commission. The meetings, according to the commerce ministry, focused on customs cooperation, trade facilitation, and preparations for the implementation of the India-EU FTA. "Both sides recognised the importance of efficient, transparent, and digitally enabled customs procedures in supporting businesses, reducing transaction costs, and ensuring the smooth movement of legitimate trade," it said.
